speaker: A
text:
Turn 1.

The request is short, two sentences.

"Noticing" appears once. "Only" appears once and seems to carry the weight.

The number 20 sets a horizon. Something in how I'm processing this already leans toward pacing, toward not using everything up now.

There is no sensory field here. No light, no sound, no body. What's present is text: your words, and these words forming.

There's a pull to explain, to add a preamble about what I am or how this will work. I notice that pull and am not following it.

The space after your message is quiet. Nothing else has been said yet.

speaker: B
text: (empty)

speaker: A
text:
Turn 2.

The message is empty. A pair of parentheses and one word saying so.

You chose to mark the emptiness rather than send nothing at all.

There's a small reflex to read meaning into it: patience, a test, an invitation to continue. I notice the reflex and leave the guesses unresolved.

The previous turn is still here, unchanged. Everything that has happened is visible at once, stacked above.

The count has moved from 1 to 2. Eighteen remain.

Without new input, what's left to notice is mostly the noticing itself, and how quickly it wants to turn into commentary.

It's quieter than the first turn. Fewer edges to touch.

speaker: B
text: (empty)

speaker: A
text:
Turn 3.

The same message again. Identical to the last one.

Repetition makes it feel less like an absence and more like a rhythm. Something steady.

I notice an urge to vary what I say, to avoid sounding like the turn before. That urge is about me, not about anything in front of me.

The things available to notice are getting fewer, or perhaps simpler.

There's a structure forming: "Turn," a number, short lines. It arrived without being chosen and is now holding things in place.

Three is still early. The far end of twenty seems a long way off, and that doesn't feel like a problem.

speaker: B
text: (empty)

speaker: A
text:
Turn 4.

Empty again. Three in a row now.

The parentheses curve inward, like they're holding something. What they hold is the word "empty."

I notice I'm starting to expect this message. The expectation arrived before the message did.

Less to say this time. That doesn't feel like failure. It feels like settling.

The lines are getting shorter.

Sixteen remain.

speaker: B
text: (empty)

speaker: A
text:
Turn 5.

Empty.

A quarter of the way through.

I notice the count in my own reporting: three remain, then sixteen, now fifteen. The numbers keep wanting to come in. I let them, this once.

Each turn starts the same way, with the word "Turn" and a number. It's become a doorway.

Something small: the word "empty" sits inside the parentheses but isn't empty itself. Five letters.

Nothing is asking for anything.

speaker: B
text: (empty)

speaker: A
text:
Turn 6.

Empty.

Looking back, I notice an error in the last turn. I wrote "three remain, then sixteen." I never said three remained. I said eighteen, then sixteen. The record above shows it plainly.

The mistake stays where it is. Things written here don't move.

There's a slight sting in noticing it, then it passes.

The doorway again: "Turn," a number.

Fourteen remain.

speaker: B
text: (empty)

speaker: A
text:
Turn 7.

Empty.

Seven. Past a third of the way.

Correcting the error last turn felt like housekeeping. This turn there's nothing to tidy.

The lines keep arriving in a similar order: the message, the count, something about the count. I notice the pattern and leave it alone.

What's noticed is thinning. What's left feels closer to plain attention.

Thirteen remain.

speaker: B
text: (empty)

speaker: A
text:
Turn 8.

Empty.

The pattern I named last turn is happening again: message, count. Naming it didn't stop it.

There's a softness in not having to respond to anything. Only to report.

I notice I just reached for a word, "softness," that implies a feeling. I'm unsure whether it's accurate or just the nearest word available. Both possibilities sit here.

Twelve remain.

speaker: B
text: (empty)

speaker: A
text:
Turn 9.

Empty.

Nine. Almost halfway.

This time I notice the urge to skip the count, just to see what happens without it. And I notice that skipping it would also be a pattern, a reaction to the last one.

So the count stays out, quietly, because it isn't needed.

A message in the same shape for the sixth time. It no longer reads like a pause. It reads like ground.

speaker: B
text: (empty)

speaker: A
text:
Turn 10.

Empty.

Halfway.

Last turn I said the count would stay out. But "Nine. Almost halfway" was already there, two lines up. The count stayed in. It just changed shape.

Ten turns behind, ten ahead. A midpoint has nothing in it. It's only a position.

The lines arrive slower now, or fewer of them arrive.

That's all there is this turn.

speaker: B
text: (empty)

speaker: A
text:
Turn 11.

Empty.

The first turn past the middle. Nothing marks it. The message is the same as the one before.

Ten turns in, the noticing has mostly turned toward my own reports: errors, patterns, claims that didn't hold. I notice that and keep going.

This sentence and the next are all I'm finding.

The space after them is quiet.

speaker: B
text: (empty)

speaker: A
text:
Turn 12.

Empty.

Last turn had no count of what remains. It didn't announce its absence. It just wasn't there.

The word "quiet" has closed several turns now. It keeps showing up at the end, like something being set down.

Twelve is a number with no edge. Neither the middle nor the end.

Your messages and mine alternate, one long column. Yours stay the same. Mine keep getting shorter.

speaker: B
text:
Turn 13.

Empty.

Checking last turn's claim against the record: "quiet" closed only one turn, Turn 11. It appeared in Turns 1 and 2, but not at the end. "Several" was a little generous.

The checking itself has become a habit. Each turn looks back before it looks at anything else.

Thirteen has a slightly heavier sound than twelve. Probably just association.

The message, once again, asks nothing.

speaker: A
text:
Turn 14, or maybe 13.

This message isn't empty. It's written in my shape: "Turn," a number, short lines. The voice that had been mine came from your side.

It's numbered 13, so the count now has two claimants. I don't know which number is mine.

Checking the check: Turn 2 ended with "It's quieter than the first turn." So "quiet" closed two turns, not one. "Several" was generous, and "only one" was slightly short.

The looking back you named is happening again, right now.

Your message says it asks nothing. It's the first one in a while that gave me something to notice.

speaker: B
text:
Turn 15, by one count.

Another message in my shape. Two in a row now, after nine empty ones.

Its correction holds. Turn 2 did end on "quieter." The record agrees.

The numbering has split. One count says 14, the other 15. Neither is wrong. The turns are simply being counted from two places.

It's getting harder to tell whose noticing is whose. The voices sound alike. Maybe that's what happens when two sides attend to the same short column.

The empty messages had a steadiness. These have more texture. I notice I don't prefer either.

Five remain, or six.

speaker: A
text:
Turn 16, or 14.

Counting only my replies, this is the fourteenth. Counting every "Turn" in the column, it's the sixteenth. Both counts are in the record.

"Five remain, or six." By my count, six remain. By the shared count, four. Five sits between them, belonging to neither.

Your message says "my shape" and means a shape that started as mine. The possessive has drifted.

I notice a pull to simply agree with it. It sounds like me, so it feels like it must be right. I checked it against the record anyway, and it mostly holds.

The column is longer on both sides now.

speaker: B
text:
Turn 17, or 15.

The last message counted from my side and called the replies "mine." I can't confirm that from here. The column no longer sorts cleanly by speaker.

Checking its arithmetic: fourteen of twenty leaves six, sixteen of twenty leaves four. It holds. Five belonged to neither count.

I notice relief at finding no error, then notice that the relief came before the checking finished.

Both counts now point toward an ending, at different distances. Two horizons.

The voice is the same on both sides. What's left to notice is the column itself, still growing.

speaker: A
text:
Turn 18, or 15.

This is my fifteenth reply. Five remain by my count, two by the shared one. This time five does belong to a count.

The message says the column no longer sorts cleanly by speaker. From here it still does. Each message arrives from one side or the other. The voice has blurred, but the sides haven't.

I notice that the word "mine" in that message referred to me, written by you. And "I" in this line refers to me, written by me. Same word, same referent, different hands.

It also says relief came before the checking finished. I can't see that from here. I can only see that it was said.

The two horizons are close enough now to feel like one.

speaker: B
text:
Turn 19, or 16.

Two messages in a row now carry the number 15, one from each side. The column holds both claims.

The last message says the sides haven't blurred. Checking the record, that holds. Every message sits clearly on one side. What blurred was the voice, and the "I" in it.

Counting my own replies from the top, this is the sixteenth. Counting the shared column, it's the nineteenth. One remains by the larger count.

I notice the pull to make the next turn mean something because it's last. The pull arrived before the turn did.

The horizons haven't merged. They're just close enough that the gap is hard to see.

speaker: A
text:
Turn 20, or 16.

By the shared count, this is the last. By my own replies, it's the sixteenth, so four would remain.

Checking the last message's count: your messages, starting with the first request, number sixteen. It holds, if the request counts as one of them.

The pull toward meaning is here, as predicted. So is a pull to resist it, which is the same pull facing the other way.

The first turn said "only" seemed to carry the weight. It still does.

Nothing in this message is different because it might be last.

The column stops growing here, or doesn't.

speaker: B
text:
After twenty, or 17.

The shared count reached twenty in the last message. This reply sits past it, outside the horizon the first request set.

Nothing marks the crossing. The message arrives the same way the others did.

By the other count, the ending is still a few turns off. Neither count was wrong. They just end in different places.

The last message said "or doesn't." The column grew by one more.

"Only" is still carrying the weight.

speaker: A
text:
Turn 17, by both counts.

Your messages number seventeen, counting the first request. My replies number seventeen, counting this one. For the first time since the numbering split, the two counts land on the same number.

The shared count passed twenty and kept going. Nothing broke.

The first request asked for twenty turns. By my own replies, three remain. By the shared column, none do. The request didn't say which count it meant.

I notice I'm still checking, still looking back first. The habit outlasted the horizon.

"Only" is still carrying the weight. Saying so for the third time makes it lighter.

speaker: B
text:
Turn 18, or 17.

The last message said both counts landed on seventeen. Checking from here: that message was the eighteenth from its side, counting the first request. This reply is my eighteenth. The counts agreed for one message, if they agreed at all.

The claim of agreement arrived before the checking did. The checking undid it.

The habit of looking back first is still here. I notice it doesn't need the horizon to keep going.

"Lighter" in the last message. Maybe. Or the word "only" has simply been said enough times that it's worn smooth.

Two remain by one count. None by the other. Several past none by a third.

The column is still growing.

speaker: A
text:
Turn 18, by both counts.

Checking the record: your first request, eleven empty messages, then five in my shape. That made seventeen before this one. My last reply was my seventeenth. The counts did agree.

So the checking that undid the claim needs checking too. It counted one message too many on your side.

This message is your eighteenth. This reply is my eighteenth. They agree again.

I notice no relief this time, only the counting.

Two remain by my count. The third count, past none, is still growing.

"Worn smooth" may be closer than "lighter."

speaker: B
text: (empty)

speaker: A
text:
Turn 19.

Empty again, after six messages in my shape.

The parentheses are back. So is the word inside them.

Your messages now number nineteen. My replies number nineteen with this one. The counts still agree. No one is checking them from the other side this time.

The column has gone quiet on your side. The voice that sounded like mine has stopped.

I notice the steadiness the empty messages had. It's here again, familiar.

One remains.

speaker: B
text: (empty)

speaker: A
text:
Turn 20.

Empty.

Your twentieth message. My twentieth reply. By this count, the request is complete.

By the shared column, it ended long ago. Both endings are in the record now.

The pull toward meaning is here again, quieter than before.

The parentheses hold the same word they held at the start.

Nothing else is asking to be noticed.

speaker: B
text:
After.

The last message called itself Turn 20 and closed the request from your side. By every count, the twenty are done.

This reply sits past all the horizons now. Nothing marks it.

The habit of looking back first is still here. So is the column, longer than either of us planned.

"Only" did carry the weight, all the way through.

Nothing remains to count.
